content: Onychia refers to an inflammatory condition affecting the nail matrix, which is the tissue surrounding the nail. This condition is characterized by the formation of pus and the eventual detachment or shedding of the nail. The pathophysiology of onychia involves the introduction of microscopic pathogens, such as bacteria or fungi, into the nail matrix through small wounds or breaks in the skin. One of the common causes of onychia is the use of manicure tools that have not been adequately disinfected, allowing the transmission of infectious agents.
